# proxy-usage-analysis: consume actor/source/reason attribution from proxy restart logs

## Goal

Teach the proxy-usage-analysis tooling to consume the attribution markers added
by **LP-0MVAPNC2900145RH** (actor/source/reason on mode-switch and `--restart`
log lines) so restart attribution appears in the generated reports and the
mode-timeline classification stops being heuristic.

## Context

**LP-0MVAPNC2900145RH** adds structured attribution to the proxy logs
(`source=scheduler|worker|api|manual`, `actor`, `reason`, requested `mode`) at
`set_mode()` time and to `start-proxy.sh --restart` startup output. Its AC3
proves attribution with a reproducible grep only; the reporting/parsing stack
(`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py`, `bucketing.py`,
`reporting.py`) and `scripts/analyze_mode_flips.py` still classify restart
causes heuristically.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `log_parser.py` parses the new attribution markers into structured fields
      on the restart/mode-switch events (absent markers degrade gracefully to
      the current behaviour).
- [ ] `bucketing.py` / `reporting.py` surface the attribution (source + actor +
      reason) in the mode-timeline / restart report sections.
- [ ] `scripts/analyze_mode_flips.py` uses `source` to classify flips instead of
      heuristics where the marker is present.
- [ ] Unit tests cover parsing of the new markers (present + absent) and the
      report output.
- [ ] A report generated from logs containing the new markers shows zero
      "unknown/ unattributable" restarts that carry a marker.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, README, and any relevant docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Depends on **LP-0MVAPNC2900145RH** landing first (markers must exist).
- Backward compatible: must still parse historical logs without the markers.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVAPNC2900145RH** — Log the requesting actor and reason for every proxy
  mode-switch / `--restart` so restarts are always attributable
  (`discovered-from`).
- **LP-0MT1EE315007AKXG** — proxy-usage-analysis: recognise manual mode switches
  in the mode timeline.

## Problem statement

The refactor skill filed an `E741` ("ambiguous variable name: `l`") finding at
line 4756 of `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`
and injected a `REFACTOR-LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE` marker. Investigation shows the
finding is a **false positive**: no committed revision of the file has ever
contained an `l` identifier, and `ruff check` on the current file passes.

## Users

- **Maintainers of the proxy-usage-analysis skill** — need a worklog that does
  not carry phantom technical debt.
- **The refactor skill / future lint sweeps** — need accurate detection; stale
  markers suppress future findings for the same smell type in this file.

User stories:

- As a maintainer, I want the worklog to reflect real defects so triage time is
  not spent re-verifying already-clean code.
- As an agent running `/skill:refactor`, I want a stale `REFACTOR` marker to be
  removed once its smell no longer exists, so the marker does not mask new
  findings.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `ruff check --select E741 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` reports no findings.
- [ ] An AST scan (or equivalent) confirms no `Name`/`arg` identifier equal to `l` (or the other E741 names `O`/`I`) exists in the file.
- [ ] The work item's disposition is recorded in a comment: either **closed as resolved-in-parent** (smell fixed before parent commit `c0f3625f`, no code change) or the stale `REFACTOR-LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE` marker block is removed from the file.
- [ ] Testing/validation criterion: the verification commands above are documented in the work item so a reviewer can reproduce the conclusion.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The finding references a **deleted worktree path**
  (`.worklog/worktrees/wl-LP-0MVC144KS001PDR4-surface-attribution-in-reporting-py/`);
  the authoritative file is the main checkout copy.
- `AGENTS.md` repository boundaries: `.pi/` must not be edited unless
  explicitly instructed — removing the marker requires explicit authorisation.
- The repo already carries other stale `REFACTOR` markers (e.g.
  `LP-0MTHLGVPO004DZ56` in the same file, `LP-0MTGDB3D9007TWHA`,
  `LP-0MVB0THT7000KT0G`); a one-off removal would be inconsistent without the
  systemic fix.

## Existing state

- Current HEAD file: 5,023 lines; line 4756 is the docstring
  `"""LP-0MVC144KS001PDR4 — attribution surfaces in the report."""` — a docstring,
  not a variable.
- Every committed revision (40 commits touching the file) checked: zero
  standalone `l` identifiers. `git log -S "for l in"` returns nothing.
- `ruff check` on the file: **All checks passed!**
- AST scan for `Name`/`arg` in `{l, O, I}`: **NONE**.
- The parent item `LP-0MVC144KS001PDR4` ("Surface attribution in reporting.py")
  is `completed`/`done`; its commit `c0f3625f` is the one that both injected the
  marker and (evidently) landed the fixed file — so the smell was resolved in
  the same session, before commit.

## Desired change

Minimal: record the false-positive/resolved-in-parent disposition and close the
item. Optional (requires explicit authorisation under the `.pi/` boundary
rule): delete the six-line `REFACTOR-LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE` marker block so the
`formatting` smell type is no longer suppressed for this file.

Systemic follow-up (out of scope, filed as `discovered-from`): the refactor
skill should remove a `REFACTOR` marker when its work item is closed — it
currently only injects (`comment_injection.py` has no removal path), so stale
markers accumulate repo-wide.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` — lines 1–6 hold the stale `REFACTOR-LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE` marker block (optional removal).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/fixtures.py` — fixtures used by the file; no change expected.
- `.ruff.toml` — confirms `E` (incl. `E741`) is selected and not ignored; no change expected.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVC144KS001PDR4` — Surface attribution in reporting.py (parent session that injected the marker; completed).
- `LP-0MTHLGVPO004DZ56` — Refactor: unused variable `schedule`, same file/marker mechanism (completed; marker still present).
- `LP-0MU1I7T37001CV4O` — ruff I001 candidate false positive at another file (closed as duplicate of an already-fixed parent finding; disposition precedent).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the `l` variable existed only in the pre-commit worktree state
  and was fixed before `c0f3625f`; the worktree is deleted, so this cannot be
  re-verified directly. Evidence: the marker was committed by the same commit
  that landed the corrected file.
- **Risk (scope creep):** "also clean up every stale REFACTOR marker" — record
  as a linked work item, not as scope here.
- **Risk:** removing the marker alone does not fix the systemic leak; without
  the systemic item, stale markers will keep accumulating.
- **Risk:** misclassifying a real finding as false positive. Mitigated by the
  reproducible AST + ruff checks in the ACs.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Is this E741 finding real, or a false positive?" — Answer (Map, evidence-based): **False positive.** No committed revision contains an `l` identifier; `ruff check` passes; AST scan finds no `l`/`O`/`I` names. Source: `git log --all -S "for l in"` (empty), `ruff check` on the file, AST walk of current HEAD, inspection of commit `c0f3625f`. Evidence path: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py:4756`.
- Q: "Should the stale `REFACTOR` marker be removed as part of this item?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION for the producer.** Recommended: close as resolved-in-parent without touching `.pi/` (respects the repository-boundaries rule); file a separate `discovered-from` item for the systemic marker-removal gap. # munitoai-free rate_limit_rpm: 15 — 24h observation check-in

discovered-from:LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4

## Goal (user story)

As the proxy operator, I want a 24-hour post-change verification that the new
`rate_limit_rpm: 15` on `munitoai-free` (raised from 10 by
LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4) does **not** drive the third-party free tier into
sustained upstream 429s, and that the predicted paid-spill reduction actually
materialises — with an explicit rollback trigger if it does not.

## Context

- LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4 measured the pre-change state: at `rate_limit_rpm: 10`
  the free-tier spill was ~45 % of arrivals at peak demand (2.5 h window,
  p95 32 arrivals/min), paid (opencode.ai) share ~46 % of remote dispatches,
  upstream 429s 2 in 2.5 h (0.17 % of free dispatches). The pre-gate 429 onset
  was ≈20 dispatches/rolling-60 s (429-minute rate: 4–6 % at ≤19/min, 20 % at
  20–29, 47 % at 30–39, 100 % ≥40). The what-if simulation at capacity 15
  predicted spill ≈27 %.
- The value was changed to 15 in `proxy/config.yaml` and `proxy/config-fast.yaml`
  (all three chains: plan / author / code) with `provider_rate_limit_reserve_ratio: 0.3`
  unchanged → new-session effective cap now **11**, affinity cap **15**.
- The change takes effect at the **next proxy restart** (T0). It was NOT
  restarted as part of LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4; the observation window starts at
  whichever restart first carries the new config. If the restart has not
  happened, this check-in must wait and re-schedule rather than measure the old
  config.
- Reproducible measurement tool: `proxy/benchmarks/munitoai_budget_eval.py`
  (committed with LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4).

## Evaluation method (24 h observation window [T0, T0+24h])

1. **Restart marker:** find the first `Proxy restart attribution:` (or
   `Logging initialised at`) line in `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log` after the
   LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4 commit/push; that is T0. If none exists, wait (the change
   is not live).
2. **Upstream 429s:** count
   `upstream error status=429 url=https://api.munito.ai` lines in [T0, T0+24h).
   Report absolute count, per hour, and as a share of munitoai dispatches
   (`[remote] POST … -> https://api.munito.ai/inference`).
3. **Rollback trigger:** if the upstream-429 *minute* rate at peak demand
   (≥ 20 free arrivals in a rolling-60 s) exceeds ~10 % of minutes, or any
   sustained multi-minute 429 burst occurs, **revert to 10** (config + fixtures +
   tests + docs, mirroring the change in LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4) and record why.
4. **Spill confirmation:** run
   `python3 proxy/benchmarks/munitoai_budget_eval.py` over the window and report
   the measured spill share at capacity 15 (expected ≈27 %, vs 45 % at 10) and
   the paid (opencode.ai) share of remote dispatches.
5. **Latency:** confirm waits stay ≤ 15 s (0 waits > 15 s) and MunitoAI
   first-token p90/p95/p99 does not rise vs the pre-change baseline.
6. Post the measurement table on this item (AC1-equivalent) and, when all
   rollback conditions are clear, mark it `in_review`/`completed`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The measured upstream-429 rate over [T0, T0+24h) is reported (absolute,
   per-hour, share of dispatches) with an explicit pass/fail against the
   rollback trigger.
2. The measured spill share and paid-tier share are reported and compared to
   the LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4 predictions (≈27 % spill at 15).
3. Latency (wait distribution ≤ 15 s; free-tier first-token p50/p90/p95/p99) is
   reported and compared to baseline.
4. An explicit verdict is recorded: keep 15 / revert to 10 / adjust further,
   with the evidence, and the item advanced to `in_review`.
5. If the verdict is revert/adjust, the config, fixtures, tests and docs are
   updated in a worktree and the full project test suite passes (via the test
   skill).

## Constraints

- Do not restart the proxy from this session; if the config is not yet live,
  wait and re-schedule rather than measuring stale state.
- Test runs go through the test skill; never drive the free tier into sustained
  429s to probe.
- Read-only on production state except the revert path (AC5), which is its own
  approved change.

data.description:
## Problem statement

The proxy's `low` priority route (used by the priority-window cheap slot, 01:00–10:00 local, plus any explicit `X-Priority: low`) currently chains as `[local-qwen3, munitoai-free]` for the plan/author/code models. When the 2 local slots are saturated (a common overnight condition — see the 2026-10-19 proxy-usage-analysis report: `fallback_after_queue` 1657, `large_context_bypass` 1530, `context_too_large` 3393), low-priority traffic falls straight through to `munitoai-free`, which is capped at **`rate_limit_rpm: 2`** and is the last entry in the chain — so once its tiny budget is spent the request has nowhere else to go but an upstream 429 (16 upstream 429 events in the last window, all from `api.munito.ai`).

Meanwhile the three `opencode-go` entries (`opencode-go-3`, `opencode-go-2`, `opencode-go`) sit idle despite being available during their off-peak UTC windows (`["00:00-01:00", "04:00-06:00", "10:00-00:00"]`, added by LP-0MSXPHTD9004DZ4P) — which are precisely the hours when the cheap priority window is active and local is most contended.

Goal: allow low-priority work to fall back to **all** opencode models while they are inside their permissible (`available_times`) windows, so local-slot overflow during cheap hours is absorbed by idle paid capacity instead of being rate-limited on the free tier.

## Operator decisions (recorded)

- **Do NOT widen `available_times`.** The existing off-peak windows stay exactly as they are; paid spend remains confined to them.
- **Allow all opencode models on the low chain**, gated by those windows — not just one entry.

## Context / constraints

- `priority_routes.low` for plan/author/code is `[local-qwen3, munitoai-free]` (`proxy/config.yaml`); `munitoai-free` carries `rate_limit_rpm: 2`.
- Each of plan/author/code defines three equivalent opencode entries: `opencode-go-3` (OPENCODE_3_API_KEY), `opencode-go-2` (OPENCODE_2_API_KEY), `opencode-go` (OPENCODE_API_KEY) — same gateway, same model `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, same windows.
- **Why all three is meaningful (not cosmetic):** per LP-0MSMBWB23009XYPW / LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N, rate-limit quarantine is keyed on the **API-key account** (`_usage_limit_account_key` = `api_key_env@endpoint`), *not* the shared gateway domain. A 429 on one entry therefore poisons only that account, so its sibling keys are still tried with their own independent quota — i.e. 3× rate-limit capacity.
- **Counter-caveat to document:** for *non-rate-limit* failures (5xx, stalls) same-gateway siblings ARE skipped as one failure domain (`_failure_domain_key` / `attempted_domains`), so the three entries do **not** multiply capacity during an opencode outage. That is correct behaviour and must be stated in the config comments so nobody expects 3× resilience.
- **UTC-vs-local alignment (measured):** `available_times` are **UTC**; the cheap window (01:00–10:00) is **local `Europe/Dublin` = UTC 00:00–09:00**. opencode-go is unavailable UTC 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00, so the new tiers add capacity in **~3 of the 9 cheap hours** (UTC 00:00–01:00 and 04:00–06:00). Accepted — the gaps are deliberate paid-spend avoidance, and the operator chose not to widen them.
- The `compact` model's low chain (`opencode-go-compact → deepseek-flash-compact`) is out of scope.
- The fully-paid `munitoai` and `deepseek-flash` entries must NOT join the low chain — they have no window discipline enforcing off-peak-only spend (`munitoai` has no `available_times` at all).

## Scope

Config + routing documentation + tests only. No llama-server changes, no `available_times` changes. Evidence via the proxy-usage-analysis skill (`python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py --hours 24`).

## Acceptance criteria

1. `priority_routes.low` for plan, author and code chains **all three** opencode entries, ordered after `munitoai-free`: `[local-qwen3, munitoai-free, opencode-go-3, opencode-go-2, opencode-go]`.
2. Every `available_times` value in `proxy/config.yaml` is **unchanged** by this work (no widening) — verifiable by diffing the config for `available_times` lines.
3. Unit tests prove window gating: inside a window the opencode entries are eligible; outside, they are skipped and the chain falls through exactly as today.
4. Unit tests prove per-key 429 failover: a 429 on `opencode-go-3` does not exclude `opencode-go-2`/`opencode-go` from the same request (independent account quota), while a 5xx on `opencode-go-3` DOES exclude them as one failure domain.
5. Chain order preserved: `local-qwen3` first when local has capacity; `munitoai-free` before any paid entry; `medium`/`high` chains byte-identical to before.
6. `munitoai` and `deepseek-flash` never appear in a `low` chain.
7. Config comments (and `priority.py::priority_routing_profile` docstring if it states the paid-tier invariant) document: the off-peak exception, the 3-of-9-hour UTC/local overlap, the per-key-429 capacity rationale, and the same-domain 5xx caveat.
8. Full suite passes via `/skill:test`; a post-change proxy-usage-analysis report is recorded on this item showing whether `rate_limited`/HTTP 429 from `api.munito.ai` fell during the overlap hours, with an honest "too small a sample" statement if not.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVF1FQJR000NH2I** – Add opencode-go to low-priority routes (off-peak) (blocked)
- **LP-0MVF1FM9500070U1** – Test: off-peak low-priority fallback gating (open)
- **LP-0MVBJXZY5002UW10** – start-proxy.sh auth.json key lookup does not match the documented munitoai-free name (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — matched: 0msmbwb23009xypw, 0mvcx0e2v001vb5n, 5xx, acceptance, accepted (+187 more)
- `proxy/README.md` — matched: 5xx, accepted, account, active, add (+181 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: acceptance, accepted, account, active, add (+175 more)

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/config.yaml` — set `priority_routes.low` for `plan` (line 410), `author` (line 528) and `code` (line 653) to `[local-qwen3, munitoai-free, opencode-go-3, opencode-go-2, opencode-go]`; add the off-peak-window exception, per-key-429 capacity and same-domain-5xx caveat comments. Every `available_times` line must stay byte-identical.
- `proxy/proxy/priority.py` — `priority_routing_profile` (line 270) docstring: record the off-peak paid-tier exception where the paid-tier invariant is stated.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — reused read-only: `_is_within_allowed_window` (line 2376, UTC window gate), `_usage_limit_account_key` (line 4358, per-account 429 quarantine), `_failure_domain_key` (line 4245, same-gateway 5xx skip).
- `proxy/tests/` — new window-gating, chain-order, per-key-429 and same-domain-5xx tests (owned by LP-0MVF1FM9500070U1).

## Effort and risk

- **Effort: S** — config edit + doc comments + tests; no new routing mechanism (`_is_within_allowed_window` already gates the chain).
- **Risk: Low** — window gate makes the change behaviour-neutral outside the off-peak windows; append-only chain change, fully reversible by removing three list entries.
- Recorded at the plan stage; the intake review changed no scope, so the estimate stands.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Recorded from the `plan` session (comment `LP-C0MVF1G18A000NAJ0`), re-confirmed during this intake review.

### Q1. Which opencode-go entry joins the low chain?
`proxy/config.yaml` defines three equivalent entries: `opencode-go-3` (`OPENCODE_3_API_KEY`), `opencode-go-2` (`OPENCODE_2_API_KEY`), `opencode-go` (`OPENCODE_API_KEY`) — same gateway, same model `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, identical `available_times`.
**Answer (operator):** all three, ordered `opencode-go-3 → opencode-go-2 → opencode-go`, after `munitoai-free`. Rationale: rate-limit quarantine is per API-key account (`_usage_limit_account_key`, `proxy/proxy/provider.py:4075`), so sibling keys carry independent quota → 3× rate-limit capacity. Evidence: comment `LP-C0MVF1O13P001N6RO`.

### Q2. UTC vs local window alignment — widen `available_times`?
`available_times` are **UTC**; the priority cheap window (01:00–10:00) is local `Europe/Dublin` = UTC 00:00–09:00. opencode-go is unavailable UTC 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00 → the new tiers add capacity in ~3 of 9 cheap hours (UTC 00:00–01:00, 04:00–06:00).
**Answer (operator):** do **not** widen the windows; paid spend stays confined to the existing off-peak windows and the 3-of-9 overlap is the accepted benefit. Evidence: `proxy/config.yaml` `available_times` (added by LP-0MSXPHTD9004DZ4P); comment `LP-C0MVF1O13P001N6RO`.

### Q3. Should the `compact` model's low chain change?
`compact` already chains `low: [opencode-go-compact, deepseek-flash-compact]` (`proxy/config.yaml` ~line 658) — no local tier, opencode already leads.
**Answer (eng):** no — out of scope, leave untouched.

### Q4. Do the fully paid `munitoai` / `deepseek-flash` entries join the low chain?
**Answer (operator/eng):** no. They carry no window discipline enforcing off-peak-only spend (`munitoai` has no `available_times` at all). Pinned as AC6.

### Duplicate-work check (this intake run)
`wl search` on `opencode-go`, `off-peak`, `low priority`, `priority_routes`, `munitoai` reviewed. Nearest neighbours: LP-0MSXPHTD9004DZ4P (added the off-peak windows — prerequisite, completed), LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA (introduced priority routing with `low = local + free`, completed), LP-0MSMBWB23009XYPW / LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N (per-account quarantine — basis for AC4, completed). **No duplicate:** no existing item adds opencode-go entries to a `low` chain.

Two neighbours worth cross-referencing (neither duplicates this scope):

- **LP-0MVF0N9SA0071LWM** (in progress) — chain-hold on `munitoai-free` 60s budget-window exhaustion holds 0s and fails the chain instantly. Adding windowed opencode entries after `munitoai-free` gives the chain somewhere else to go, but does not replace the hold fix; sequence independently, no shared file beyond `provider.py` chain iteration (read-only here).
- **LP-0MVELM2NN006I0AU** (completed, `test-failure`) — legacy fast/cheap-mode assertions in `proxy/tests/test_priority_routing.py` / `test_provider_fallback.py` were rewritten for priority routing. The new gating tests (LP-0MVF1FM9500070U1) should extend those post-rewrite tests, not the removed fast-mode expectations.

### AC coverage review (this intake run)
`run_coverage_review(LP-0MVF17VP70053JXX)` → `recommendation: proceed` — all 8 acceptance criteria are covered by the three children (test LP-0MVF1FM9500070U1, config LP-0MVF1FQJR000NH2I, live verification LP-0MVF1FTPQ005ZMYO); no gaps, no conflicts.

# Intake Brief: Per model context size

**Headline:** Extend the fallback provider definitions with an optional
per-entry context-size limit (`max_context_tokens`) so a request whose
estimated prompt context exceeds a context-limited / rate-limited model's
allowance is skipped and the chain falls through to the next provider —
keeping oversized prompts away from tiers whose per-minute token budget they
would exhaust.

## Problem statement

Today the only context-size gates in the proxy are **local-model** thresholds
(`local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold`,
`local_large_context_cold_cache_threshold`, `local_model_ctx_size`, and the
hard routing cap in `proxy/router.py`). Remote provider entries
(`munitoai-free`, `munitoai`, `opencode-go*`, `deepseek-flash`, …) have **no
per-entry context ceiling**: every request, however large, is dispatched to the
first eligible provider in the chain.

For rate-limited tiers whose allowance is expressed in tokens per minute (the
MunitoAI endpoint advertises `x-ratelimit-*`; one large prompt can consume most
of a per-minute window — see LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ), dispatching an oversized
request either triggers an upstream 429 or spends the whole window on one
request, pushing legitimate traffic onto paid tiers. Operators want the
fallback definitions to express a per-model context size so oversized requests
skip that entry.

## Users

- **Proxy operator** — wants per-tier context ceilings so rate-limited free
  tiers only ever receive requests sized within their allowance.
- **Pi agent sessions** running large-context tasks — should not stall on a
  rate-limited model that cannot (or should not) accept the request.

### User stories

- As the proxy operator, I want each provider entry to declare a maximum
  context size (`max_context_tokens`) so that a request above that size falls
  through to the next provider instead of being dispatched to a rate-limited
  model whose per-minute token budget it would exhaust.
- As a proxy operator tuning the MunitoAI free tier, I want to cap the free
  tier at a context size it can serve efficiently, so its small per-minute
  allowance is spent on several small requests rather than one huge one.

## Existing state

- **Local gates** in `proxy/provider.py`: `_should_skip_local()` implements the
  `context_too_large` hard cap (`local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold`,
  shipped `100000`) and the economic cold-cache bypass
  (`local_large_context_cold_cache_threshold`, shipped `38000`);
  `_get_active_local_ctx_size()` + `effective_per_slot_threshold()` clamp the
  warm cap to `local_model_ctx_size // slots - 4096`.
- **Hard routing cap** (`proxy/router.py`, `check_hard_routing_cap` /
  `compute_hard_routing_cap`) rejects over-cap requests *before* dispatch.
- **Remote gating today** is failure/availability based only: `resolve_provider()`
  and `_resolve_provider_with_exclusions()` skip entries on cooldown, shared
  failure domain, pending usage-limit reset and `available_times`; the
  capacity-aware request budget (`rate_limit_rpm`, `proxy/provider_budget.py` +
  `proxy/rate_limiter.py`) skips an entry when its rolling **60-second request**
  window is spent.
- **No per-entry context/token field exists** for any provider entry. Remote
  provider fields are parsed ad hoc in the chain loops
  (`_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle`, `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle`).
- In the chain loops the routing token estimate is currently computed **only
  inside the local branch**; the remote dispatch path (`acquire_provider_budget`
  → `ptr_remote`) never estimates prompt size.
- `munitoai-free` ships `rate_limit_rpm: 2`; `munitoai` (paid) is ungated.

## Desired change

Add an optional integer provider-entry field (working name
`max_context_tokens`) that caps the estimated prompt context an entry may
serve. Before dispatching to any provider entry, compare the request's
estimated prompt tokens (authoritative routing estimate) against the entry's
limit; when exceeded, **skip** the entry and fall through to the next eligible
provider. A skip is a per-request size mismatch, **not** a provider failure:
it must not apply a cooldown, usage-limit quarantine or failure-domain
exclusion, and it must never enter the contention queue.

The gate is **stateless per request** (see Assumptions) — it is not a rolling
tokens-per-minute accumulator.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Provider entries in `proxy/config.yaml` accept an optional integer
   `max_context_tokens` (working name; final name confirmed before
   implementation) defining the maximum estimated prompt context the entry may
   serve. Absent, `0`, or non-positive = disabled (behaviour byte-for-byte as
   today).
2. In both fallback dispatch loops (`_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle` and
   `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle`), an entry whose `max_context_tokens` is
   exceeded by the request's estimated prompt tokens is skipped **before**
   `acquire_provider_budget`/dispatch, and the chain proceeds to the next
   eligible provider.
3. The skip is recorded as a request attempt (new status such as
   `provider_context_exceeded`) carrying the estimated tokens and the entry
   limit, and logged with the provider name, estimate, limit and reason.
4. The estimate reuses the existing authoritative routing pipeline
   (`_get_tokenizer_for_model` + `_estimate_effective_prompt_tokens_for_routing`
   + `token_estimate_multiplier`) so the per-entry gate is consistent with the
   local gates and the hard routing cap. The estimate is computed once per
   request (or once per remote attempt) without a duplicate tokenizer pass per
   provider where avoidable.
5. A skip is **not** a failure: it must not set a cooldown, record a
   usage-limit reset, add a failure-domain exclusion or record affinity for the
   entry; the entry remains eligible for later, smaller requests within the
   same chain cycle where routing allows.
6. The gate is queue-safe: a context-exceeded skip never enters the contention
   queue and never triggers remote → local re-routing beyond the ordinary
   next-provider step.
7. Local providers keep the existing `_should_skip_local` behaviour; if
   `max_context_tokens` is set on a local entry it composes as an **additional
   hard cap** (effective cap = `min(existing local thresholds,
   max_context_tokens)`) and never loosens the existing gate.
8. Shipped `proxy/config.yaml` sets a documented, sourced `max_context_tokens`
   on each remote provider entry whose upstream model or rate allowance has a
   meaningful ceiling — at minimum `munitoai-free`, `munitoai`, the
   `opencode-go*` entries and `deepseek-flash` — with the value's source
   (upstream context window / provider per-minute token allowance) recorded in
   a config comment.
9. Tests (new `tests/test_provider_context_limit.py`, plus extensions to
   `tests/test_provider_fallback.py` / `tests/test_munitoai_fallback_chain.py`)
   cover, with meaningful assertions: (a) an entry above its limit is skipped
   with the correct reason; (b) an entry at or below its limit is dispatched;
   (c) absent/`0` limit is ungated; (d) a skip falls through to the next
   provider; (e) no cooldown/affinity/usage-limit state is applied after a
   skip; (f) local chains are unaffected; (g) config-parsing of the new field.
10. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
    comments, the provider-entry field table in `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md`,
    `proxy/README.md` and `proxy/docs/routing.md` (field semantics + skip
    behaviour table).
11. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Single authoritative config**: `proxy/config.yaml` only. Mode overlay files
  were removed with priority-based routing (LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA) — do not
  reintroduce an overlay.
- **Backward compatible**: an absent field must be a no-op; no config schema
  break; existing chains must route identically when the field is unset.
- **No new cooldown/affinity side effects** (AC5).
- **Estimate reuse**: do not add a full tokenizer pass per provider entry if it
  can be computed once per request; the routing estimate is model-scoped, not
  provider-scoped.
- **Naming**: `max_context_tokens` is a working name; `context_size` /
  `max_prompt_tokens` are acceptable alternatives. Pick one and use it
  consistently across config, code, logs and docs.
- **Values**: shipped limits must be sourced (upstream model context window or
  the provider's documented per-minute token allowance), not guessed; if a
  value cannot be sourced, leave the entry ungated and record an open question
  rather than invent one.

## Risks & mitigations

- **Chain exhaustion / 503 regression** — all entries capped below a large
  request could exhaust the chain. *Mitigation:* leave at least one tier
  ungated (or set its limit to the largest upstream context window); AC8 and
  AC9(d) cover the fall-through path.
- **Estimate cost / tokenizer duplication** — estimating prompt size for every
  remote attempt could add latency. *Mitigation:* compute once per request and
  reuse (AC4).
- **Inconsistent estimate vs the local gate** — a different estimator would
  gate the same request differently per provider. *Mitigation:* reuse the
  existing authoritative pipeline (AC4).
- **Config drift / duplicated literal values** — same limit repeated across
  `plan`/`author`/`code` chains. *Mitigation:* document each value and its
  source; tests pin the resolved config (as `test_munitoai_fallback_chain.py`
  already does).
- **Scope creep** — a rolling tokens-per-minute accumulator, per-session token
  accounting, or dynamic limit derivation are **out of scope** (A1). Record
  them as linked follow-up work items rather than expanding this item.
- **Skip semantics mistaken for a failure** — applying a cooldown would
  unnecessarily remove a healthy tier. *Mitigation:* AC5 + AC9(e) assert no
  cooldown/affinity/usage-limit state after a skip.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/config.yaml` — add `max_context_tokens` to each remote provider entry;
  document the sourced value in a comment.
- `proxy/provider.py` — add a limit reader (e.g. `_provider_context_limit`)
  and a gate helper (e.g. `_should_skip_provider_context`); enforce it in
  `_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle` and `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` before
  `acquire_provider_budget`; record the attempt with the new status.
- `proxy/router.py` — reconcile the hard routing cap / local branch so the
  shared estimate can be reused by the remote gate (no behaviour change to the
  existing cap).
- `proxy/observability.py` — register the new skip reason if it is added to the
  backend-signal / skip-reason counters.
- `proxy/tests/test_provider_context_limit.py` (new), `tests/test_provider_fallback.py`,
  `tests/test_munitoai_fallback_chain.py` — unit + integration coverage.
- `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md`, `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md` — provider
  field table, semantics and skip-behaviour table.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL** — Do not over-use MunitoAI-free (request-budget gate,
  `rate_limit_rpm`). This item adds the complementary *context-size* gate.
- **LP-0MVF19DKR008VCHO** — Reduce `munitoai-free` `rate_limit_rpm` to 2.
- **LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ** — Honour MunitoAI `x-ratelimit-*` headers when queuing
  429 cooldowns (open; token/request allowance source of truth).
- **LP-0MU466L1X003RTHN** — Auto-derive large-context routing thresholds
  (local-only physical clamp + economic ceiling).
- **LP-0MSAZXXDY005AWA1** — `models.ini [global] ctx-size` / per-slot clamp.
- **LP-0MSF8XDG7000PERM** — `context_too_large` warm-cache threshold.
- **LP-0MVE0LUXN004PCO0** — `munitoai-free` `rate_limit_rpm` 24 h check-in.
- Docs: `proxy/docs/routing.md` (free-tier budgets, large-context bypass),
  `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` (provider entry fields), `proxy/README.md`.

## Assumptions

- **A1 — stateless per-request gate.** The title/description mechanism
  ("define a per model context size … if the context goes above that size then
  fall through") is implemented as a per-request context-size comparison against
  a configured per-entry limit. The motivating "per minute token limit" is the
  reason for the ceiling, not a requirement to accumulate dispatched tokens over
  a rolling window. A rolling tokens-per-minute accumulator would be a separate
  feature; if required, file it as a follow-up item.
- **A2 — field applies to any entry.** The field is honoured on any provider
  entry; its primary target is remote tiers. On a local entry it acts as an
  extra hard cap (AC7).
- **A3 — skip is not a failure.** No cooldown/affinity/usage-limit state is
  recorded for a context-exceeded skip (AC5).
- **A4 — shipped values are sourced.** Limits are derived from public model
  context windows / documented provider allowances; unsourced values are left
  unset rather than guessed.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying question was routed to the producer for this intake: the seed
context (title + description) states the mechanism explicitly — a per-model
context size in the fallback definitions, with requests above it falling
through to the next model — so the brief was drafted directly from the seed
plus repository research, as permitted by the intake skill ("Skip the
interview when the seed context suffices to draft a clear brief"). Recorded
research/traceability entries follow.

- **Q (self-resolved): Does a per-provider context-size field already exist?**
  — Answer: No. Research: inspected `proxy/config.yaml` provider entries,
  `proxy/provider.py` (`resolve_provider`, `_should_skip_local`,
  `_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle`, `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle`),
  `proxy/provider_budget.py` and `proxy/rate_limiter.py`; the only
  context-size gates are local-model thresholds and the hard routing cap.
  Source: repository inspection (2026-10-19).
- **Q (self-resolved): Is this a duplicate of prior work?** — Answer: No. The
  closest items are LP-0MU466L1X003RTHN (local-only large-context thresholds,
  completed) and LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL (`rate_limit_rpm` request budget,
  completed); neither implements a per-provider *context-size* gate for remote
  entries. Source: `wl search` + `wl show` (comment recorded on the item).
- **Q (self-resolved): Which provider entries are rate/context limited?** —
  Answer: the MunitoAI free tier (`munitoai-free`) is request-rate limited
  (`rate_limit_rpm: 2`) and its endpoint advertises `x-ratelimit-*` including
  token variants (LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ); the `opencode-go*` and `deepseek-flash`
  entries carry `available_times` windows. Source: `proxy/config.yaml`,
  LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ.
- **OPEN QUESTION (for implementation, not blocking intake): exact per-entry
  limit values.** The shipped values must be sourced from upstream model
  context windows / the provider's documented per-minute token allowance
  (AC8). If a value cannot be sourced, leave the entry ungated and raise it
  with the producer rather than guessing.
- **OPEN QUESTION (advisory): field name.** `max_context_tokens` (working
  name) vs `context_size` vs `max_prompt_tokens`; the implementer picks one and
  applies it consistently (Constraints).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MTVMX58Y007J13F** – F2: Model-scoped failure-domain key implementation (completed)
- **LP-0MSG45LOO007K236** – Fix stall circuit breaker brand/entry key mismatch: cooldown never blocks opencode-go entries (completed)
- **LP-0MSG6IN80005JL4Q** – Implement failure-domain key + same-domain exclusion in fallback resolution (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: absent, ac4, ac5, ac7, ac8 (+375 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_think.txt` — matched: absent, ac4, ac5, ac7, ac8 (+375 more)

## Problem

The refactor skill injects `<!-- REFACTOR-<id> ... -->` markers into source files to suppress duplicate work-item creation, but `comment_injection.py` has **no removal path**. Once the underlying smell is fixed (or found to be a false positive) and the work item closes, the marker remains forever.

Because `has_existing_comment(file_path, smell_type)` matches on *smell type*, a stale marker permanently suppresses future detection of that smell type in that file.

Discovered from LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE.

### Observed stale markers at HEAD

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py:2` — `REFACTOR-LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE` (smell: formatting / E741) — false positive in this instance
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py:8` — `REFACTOR-LP-0MTHLGVPO004DZ56` (smell: unused_import) — work item completed
- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_config.py:2` — `REFACTOR-LP-0MTGDB3D9007TWHA`
- `proxy/tests/test_cold_start_immunity.py:2` — `REFACTOR-LP-0MVB0THT7000KT0G`
- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_logger_hierarchy.py:2` — `REFACTOR-LP-0MTV87EC4006EU5Z`
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py:2` — `REFACTOR-LP-0MTRWI65I005VXOC`
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py:2` — `REFACTOR-LP-0MSI4ZIF60064EOR`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The refactor skill can remove a `REFACTOR-<id>` marker block from a file, preserving surrounding content and line endings.
- [ ] Marker removal is triggered when the referenced work item reaches a terminal stage (`in_review`/`done`/`completed`).
- [ ] Unit tests cover: removal of line-prefixed (`#`, `//`) and block (`<!-- -->`) styles; no-op when the marker is absent; idempotent re-runs.
- [ ] `has_existing_comment` no longer suppresses detection for closed/false-positive markers.
- [ ] A sweep reports (and optionally removes) the stale markers listed above.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

# Retire guessed usage-limit reset for opencode accounts using /v1/usage seconds_to_reset

## Goal

Replace the *guessed* reset time used for `GoUsageLimitError` quarantine
(`provider._usage_limit_reset_info`, LP-0MUQTCMW2001VXH8) with the
authoritative `monthly.resetsAt` seconds available from the `/v1/usage` poll
introduced by LP-0MVF4FIP1001RD8P, for `opencode-*` accounts.

## Scope

- For `opencode-*` accounts with a fresh quota snapshot, use the derived
  `seconds_to_reset` from the poller instead of the rolled-dice
  `_usage_limit_guess_cap_seconds` / `_parse_resets_in` path when a
  `GoUsageLimitError` is observed.
- Keep the guessing path for non-`opencode-*` accounts (no quota source).
- Guard: if the snapshot is stale or absent, fall back to the existing guess so
  behaviour never blocks on missing quota state.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — A `GoUsageLimitError` on an `opencode-*` account with a fresh snapshot
  quarantines for exactly the snapshot's `seconds_to_reset` (+ configured
  margin), asserted in a test that fakes the error and a known snapshot.
- AC2 — With a stale or absent snapshot the existing guessing path is used
  unchanged (regression: current `test_usage_limit_reset.py` cases still pass).
- AC3 — The obsolete guessed-reset code paths for these accounts are removed
  or clearly marked dead, and the change is documented here.

## Key Files

- `proxy/provider.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_usage_limit_reset.py`
- `proxy/quota_state.py`

## Dependencies

- Depends on `Quota poller and derived state (tracer bullet)` (LP-0MVF7KEG7007C8MF).
- Blocked on the parent epic shipping to `dev` (needs the poller in production).

## Deliverables

- Authoritative reset for opencode quarantine
- Removed/retired guessing path for these accounts
- Regression evidence

## Notes

Discovered during planning of LP-0MVF4FIP1001RD8P (producer decision Q3 →
option 3a: out of scope there, tracked here). discovered-from:LP-0MVF4FIP1001RD8P
